questions.q: What four things does a minimal DAG file need, at a bare minimum?
options: An import for DAG, a with-DAG block with an ID and schedule, at least one task, and (with more than one task) a dependency line
A database connection, a DAG import, a task, and a UI theme
A Dockerfile, a requirements.txt, a DAG import, and a schedule
Only a schedule and nothing else
questions.explain: Strip away everything optional and those four pieces are what remain in a working DAG file.

questions.q: In the worked example, what does `schedule="0 0 * * *"` mean?
options: The DAG runs only when manually triggered, ignoring this value
A cron expression meaning the DAG runs once a day at midnight
The DAG is disabled and will never run
The DAG runs every 5 minutes
questions.explain: 0 0 * * * is standard cron syntax for "at minute 0 of hour 0, every day" — once daily at midnight.

questions.q: In the worked example, what's the difference between how `hello` and `world` are defined as tasks?
options: They are defined identically, with no difference
world is not actually a task, only a comment
hello runs on a different Airflow instance than world
hello is a classic Operator-based task (BashOperator); world uses the @task decorator to turn a plain Python function into a task
questions.explain: The lesson shows both styles in the same DAG: instantiating an Operator directly, and using @task to decorate a function.

questions.q: Where does Airflow look for DAG files by default?
options: A folder named after the DAG's dag_id
Anywhere on the filesystem, with no configured location
Only inside the Airflow UI itself, pasted directly into a text box
The dags/ folder under $AIRFLOW_HOME
questions.explain: Airflow scans the dags/ folder under $AIRFLOW_HOME (by default) for Python files defining DAGs.

questions.q: If your DAG file has a typo, where would Airflow tell you it couldn't parse the file?
options: An import-error indicator in the DAGs list or the run's Code tab
Airflow silently ignores the file with no indication at all
It deletes the file automatically
It emails you a stack trace automatically with no UI indicator
questions.explain: Airflow surfaces parse/import errors in the DAGs list and the Code tab, rather than failing silently.
